# Phase 10 — Reproduction and research release audit

**Status: BLOCKED / NOT PASSED.** The repository rebuilt and all available software tests passed from a new Release build directory. The committed partial Phase 9 summary was regenerated byte-for-byte from the committed 19-row JSONL, and its hashes and freeze metadata match. A separate same-environment repeat now covers public-even index 8 only; it reproduces that row's formula hash, exact Ganak count, and all five system statuses. This is not a full rerun or an independent researcher's reproduction, so Phase 10 remains blocked and Phase 9 remains not passed.

## What reproduced

A clean CMake Release build with GCC 13.3.0, CMake 3.28.3, Python 3.12.3, and GMP 6.3.0 passed all **11/11 CTest targets**. The Phase 9 Python harness tests passed **13/13**. Using the exact frozen XAI and Ganak binaries, the synthetic stress suite passed **11/11** again; its compact outcome record is [`Phase-10-stress-rerun.json`](Phase-10-stress-rerun.json). These are build and software-fixture results, not new benchmark outcomes.

The Phase 10 harness regenerated `RESULT/Phase-9-public-even-partial-summary-v2.json` from `RESULT/Phase-9-public-even.jsonl`; the bytes matched exactly. It verified all row-level stdout/stderr hashes, checked the fixed 19 indices (0–36, even only), recomputed all 95 attempt statuses, and confirmed the report still says `evaluation_complete: false` and `phase9_practical_gate: false`. The original freeze manifest's **39 locked source files** match commit `a1a65b5ffdeab261bcdeaf7151c03b0c66213403`. The archive and both frozen solver executables also match their manifest hashes at the recorded local paths.

### Bounded benchmark repeat

One additional run repeated **index 8 only** on public-even, using the same decompressed formula (`600e03d4b2678d5863d0bb9fafeb27678a8b5790b0bd63ebc2d1c86d595946c6`), frozen solver binaries, commands, and resource controls. It ran from a detached checkout at the frozen code revision with the current freeze manifest and cross-split audit supplied as inputs. Ganak again returned the same exact rational count; all four XAI configurations again ended as resource limits; all five system statuses matched the original row; no mismatch occurred. Ganak's stdout changed only in the informational elapsed-time field (14.74 versus 15.25 seconds), while the exact count remained identical.

This is a **one-record same-environment smoke repeat**, selected because it was a short prior case. It does not validate the other 18 original records, the remaining public-even records, or the final-odd set; it is not independent reproduction and does not satisfy Phase 10's independence requirement. The original 19-row artifact remains untouched. The repeat JSONL is [`Phase-9-public-even-repeat-index8.jsonl`](Phase-9-public-even-repeat-index8.jsonl), its one-row summary is [`Phase-9-public-even-repeat-index8-summary.json`](Phase-9-public-even-repeat-index8-summary.json), and its selector wrapper is [`../tools/phase9_repeat_case.py`](../tools/phase9_repeat_case.py). The updated Phase 10 harness validates the row against original index 8, its internal output hashes, frozen provenance, and byte-identical summary regeneration.

## What the partial benchmark actually shows

The recorded diagnostic covers **19/98** eligible public-even records. Ganak returned exact counts on 10/19. XAI full and each of its three ablations returned **0/19**; none of the XAI configurations completed jointly with Ganak. There were no observed count mismatches among the attempted cases, but zero directly verified XAI counts and no estimable exact-match fraction. The independent exhaustive oracle was eligible for 0/19.

| System | Exact completions | Other recorded statuses |
|---|---:|---|
| Ganak | 10/19 | 6 memory limits; 3 timeouts |
| XAI full | 0/19 | 11 resource limits; 6 timeouts; 2 memory limits |
| XAI without unit propagation | 0/19 | 12 resource limits; 4 timeouts; 3 memory limits |
| XAI without components | 0/19 | 13 resource limits; 4 timeouts; 2 memory limits |
| XAI first-branch ablation | 0/19 | 11 resource limits; 7 timeouts; 1 memory limit |

Across all 95 attempts there were 10 exact completions, 47 resource-limit outcomes, 24 timeouts, and 14 memory-limit outcomes. Three attempts exceeded even 602 seconds of measured wall time, against the 600-second per-process wall limit: index 0 XAI first-branch (766,131 ms), index 0 XAI full (624,606 ms), and index 4 Ganak (814,576 ms). These remain disclosed as deviations; none of these three over-budget attempts was repeated or converted into a valid result.

The leakage audit opened odd-indexed formula bodies for its predeclared checks. It found two near-duplicate odd records, indices 173 and 177, related to public index 176; after those exclusions the audited final-odd claim set contains 95 eligible records. **No final-odd record was solver-scored or used for tuning.**

## Claims and release limits

The README, project overview, roadmap, test notes, specifications, and phase reports were checked against the artifacts. Stale repository inventories were updated to include Phases 8–10; the README now describes the 19/98 diagnostic and its zero XAI completions; the roadmap distinguishes the synthetic in-process orchestrator from a production runtime; and the orchestration and learning specifications clarify that the later leakage audit inspected odd formulas without scoring them. The public description now limits test claims to fixtures, limits benchmark statements to the reduced diagnostic, and makes no claim of general intelligence, novelty, benchmark superiority, production readiness, proof verification, or real-world safety.

The frozen protocol, archive snapshot, binary hashes, original and repeated run records, and synthetic stress artifact are available locally and identified by hashes, but the archive and solver binaries are not stored in the Git repository. The JSONL preserves outputs and resource measurements, not the decompressed formula bodies. A clean clone therefore needs the specified data and exact frozen binaries to repeat the checks; the report does not claim that a new researcher independently reproduced the historical benchmark outcomes.

## Open issues and recommendation

Phase 9 remains incomplete: 79 public-even records were not scored, the final-odd set was not solver-scored, XAI produced no exact count in the observed prefix, the independent oracle applied to none of those records, and resource-control overruns were observed. No calibration, predictive score, conformal coverage, or selective-risk estimate is available for this unlabeled counting archive. The implementation also lacks a production exact-WMC proof verifier and authenticated provenance; the Phase 8 verifier and broader orchestration tests are synthetic fixtures.

**Recommendation: narrow.** Keep the repository as a research-software artifact, but limit empirical claims to the recorded 19-case diagnostic, the single-record same-environment repeat, and synthetic software fixtures. Do not claim benchmark competence or practical XAI solver performance. Any further benchmark evaluation should use the frozen options without tuning on observed outcomes, retain input hashes and complete run outputs, enforce the declared stop limits, and be independently reproduced before a release gate is reconsidered. Any production or high-impact deployment remains a separate proposal requiring its own review.

**Phase 10 gate: BLOCKED / NOT PASSED.** This work verifies the clean build, tests, hashes, metadata, byte-identical summaries, and a one-record same-environment repeat. It does not meet the independent-reproduction requirement for the historical benchmark attempts. The Phase 10 gate is therefore not marked complete, and the Phase 9 gate remains not passed.
